feature_docs.log_area_m2: natural log of footprint area; size is the strongest single cue
feature_docs.compactness: isoperimetric quotient 4*pi*A/P^2; 1.0 is a circle, lower is sprawling
feature_docs.elongation: major/minor axis of the oriented bounding box
feature_docs.orientation_rad: dominant axis bearing, radians 0-pi; footprints align to streets
feature_docs.vertex_count: vertices in the footprint; proxies how complex the outline is
feature_docs.area_over_perimeter: A/P, a compactness proxy that is scale-aware
feature_docs.neighbour_count_50m: how many other buildings sit within 50m; dense blocks differ
feature_docs.neighbour_mean_area_50m: mean neighbour area within 50m; local grain
feature_docs.local_density_100m: buildings within 100m per hectare, a coarse urban-form signal

label: national_twins.floors
label_source: generated by seed_mumbai_metropolitan.py (random.randint), not OpenStreetMap and not survey. An earlier manifest claimed OSM crowd-sourced tags; that was wrong.
excluded_why: floors ~ height_m/3, so height would make this trivially solvable and the accuracy meaningless. A floor count readable off the height is not an estimate.
split_strategy: geographic grid cell, 0.01 deg, deterministic seed 20261004
split_rationale: random splits leak: held-out buildings sit metres from training neighbours. The geo/test gap below is the size of that leak.

not_usable_for: triage: rank buildings worth a floor survey first
any statutory, ownership or accuracy claim
fitness.verdict: No model is offered. The training label is synthetic, so no accuracy figure computed against it describes anything real. Retraining requires a genuinely observed floor count; note that the OSM path is not a substitute, because overpass._floors falls back to height_m / 3.5 when building:levels is absent, which is circular for a floors model.

model.note: no model served; load_model() gates on label_provenance_audit.json

limitations: Label authority must be confirmed per dataset; shape alone cannot establish that a label was observed rather than generated.
This estimates floors from plan shape; it cannot see height, use or structure, which is why the error band is reported.
retraction_reason: The label is a generator output. seed_mumbai_metropolitan.py sets floors = random.randint(fl_min, fl_max) and builds footprints with shapely_box from parcel dimensions, so floors is a uniform range draw and the polygons are not buildings (median 53 km2, max 3592 km2, 2.89% under 10000 m2). Every metric below was fitted against that label and describes the generator, not any city. The figures are kept only so the retraction is auditable.

reasons: within storey values 3-34, the largest bucket holds 336x the median populated bucket; a range draw leaves near-empty buckets between its spikes, which observed buildings do not
label_provenance.interpretation: This distribution is not consistent with observed buildings. It is consistent with a value drawn from a range, so any model trained on it learns the generator rather than the city.
label_provenance.generation: floors = random.randint(fl_min, fl_max) per locality; footprints = shapely_box from parcel dims

geometry_units_note: ST_Area(footprint_polygon) on SRID 4326 returns square degrees and ST_Perimeter returns coordinate units, so features named log_area_m2 and log_perimeter_m did not hold square metres or metres. This is a second, independent defect in the retracted fit.
split_note: The geographic split was itself weak: 0.01 deg produced 43523 cells for 45489 rows, so it was nearly row-random rather than neighbourhood-grouped.
